purpose: ASVS V3.7.5 had no decision. It asks that the application behave as documented when the browser lacks a security feature it depends on. Web Crypto's randomUUID and subtle are [SecureContext], so over plain HTTP or in an old enough browser they are absent - and the identifiers built from them are what the API deduplicates on. Two different undocumented behaviours existed, and neither was written down anywhere. This branch also records reasoned decisions for V3.5.4 and V3.7.4, which are blocked on deployed facts rather than on anything in the repository.
requiredInvariants: The defect has two halves and both are named. Four sites substituted Date.now() and Math.random() for a registration idempotency key, a deal command id in two different workspaces, and an invite key - turning an identifier the design assumes is unguessable into a predictable one with nothing in the record to say it happened. Five more called the missing API directly and raised a TypeError inside an event handler, which reaches the user as a control that does nothing.

The guard found two sites the manual survey missed, because `crypto?.randomUUID` does not match a grep for `crypto\\.randomUUID`. One of them, TransactionDealWorkspace, was a real second copy of the deal-command defect.

The guard's first version was too coarse and reported a false positive: it asked only whether a function mentioned Web Crypto and a weak source, and flagged a server route whose POST handler calls randomUUID() in one place and Date.now() somewhere else entirely. It now matches the three actual fallback shapes - the nullish or logical alternative, the conditional, and the early return - and a test pins that long-function case as not a finding.

Two of the files I had edited turned out to be frozen. tests/unit/platformV7RootWorkEntry.test.ts binds eight public surfaces to accepted parent 2100552142416743524f493954b6e6c86f0aa6e5 by SHA-256, and RegisterFormClientPublic.tsx and GektaChatWorkspace.tsx are two of them. Both were reverted to the accepted bytes and verified by digest. Re-hashing that register would rewrite owner-accepted evidence, which is not this programme’s to do.

That revert is why the verdict is FAIL rather than PASS. The silent-substitution half of the defect is closed everywhere, and the documented behaviour is implemented at eight surfaces - but RegisterFormClientPublic still calls randomUUID() in a render-time ref, so in a non-secure context that public page fails to render instead of saying why. Claiming PASS with a live surface unfixed would be exactly the fabricated evidence this programme forbids.

The Gekta exception could not be marked at the site for the same reason, so it lives in docs/security/browser-security-exceptions.json, where the guard reads it and rejects any entry whose reason is shorter than 80 characters. Retargeting that entry at another file leaves Gekta flagged, which a mutation proves.

A bug I introduced and then fixed: making the two registration idempotency refs lazy left them null at submit, and the `as string` cast silenced the compiler rather than the defect. They are now resolved on first submit inside a try, which also preserves the retry semantics the ref exists for - the same key is reused, and a browser that cannot produce one is refused.

A contract I documented but had not implemented: missingBrowserSecurityFeatures claimed to answer 'nothing missing' where there is no browser, but tested `typeof globalThis === 'undefined'`, which is never true in Node. It now tests `window`, and secureRandomId refuses outright when there is no browser scope, because unlike the capability report it has to produce a value.

The refusal is distinguishable from an ordinary failure, so a caller shows the right message rather than pasting the error text where a correlation id belongs. No new FailureCode was invented in OrganizationConnectForm: the intake never ran, so there is no server outcome to name.
docs/security/BROWSER_SECURITY_REQUIREMENTS.md is the documentation this requirement turns on, and it is documentation of an implemented behaviour, not in place of one.

V3.5.4 and V3.7.4 are recorded as NOT_ASSESSED with re-verifiable conditions, not left undecided. Each names the exact owner action and the KPI that follows. Their conditions pin the facts established here, so if a layer drops the preload directive or the control-host gate changes shape, the decision is re-examined rather than silently stale.
No production, REG.RU, DNS or database mutation. No registration business logic, 1C or marketing change.
acceptance: node scripts/security/verify-browser-security-capabilities.mjs exits 0: 10 files using Web Crypto, 1 excepted with a recorded reason, 0 weak fallbacks.
vitest run browserSecurityCapabilities.spec.ts browserSecurityGate.spec.tsx: 12 passed, 0 failed.
Both frozen files hash to the values the immutability register pins, checked by digest after the revert.

ASVS V3.7.5 moves NOT_ASSESSED to FAIL, naming the one surface that keeps it there: NOT_ASSESSED 39 to 38, FAIL 89 to 90, PASS unchanged at 129. V3.5.4 and V3.7.4 gain reasoned decisions with conditions that hold. Rejected decisions stay at the single pre-existing V8.2.4.
Revocable: returning a weak id rejects V3.7.5; dropping the preload directive from one HSTS layer rejects V3.7.4.
Seven negative mutations each fail a named test or make the guard exit 1, including restoring the real fallback in TransactionDealWorkspace and retargeting the exception entry.

Full apps/web vitest run: 224 failed files / 373 failed tests / 5211 passed, against a main baseline of 224 / 373 / 5199 - the baseline plus exactly the 12 new tests, with no failing file moved in either direction and the immutability register passing.
